dialog.body: City Clerk's office, this is Owen. How can I help you this morning?
Hi, yes, hello. I'm trying to figure out how to get a copy of a certificate. A birth certificate. Well, it's for my mother, actually, so I don't know if that's different.
Okay. Let's take that one piece at a time. Is the birth certificate for a person who was born here in Newport?

Yes, born in Newport. Nineteen fifty-four. Oh, and by the way, I'm standing in the drugstore right now, I'm buying batteries for the smoke detector, it started chirping at five this morning. So if you hear beeping, that's the store, not me.
That's fine, I can hear you. Those chirps are never at a good hour. So, the certificate. You're asking how to request a copy by mail?
Right, by mail. I can't really get down there during the week. Is that a form or do I just write a letter? I wasn't sure which.
There's an application form for it. You fill that out, include a copy of your photo ID, and mail it to our office here at City Hall. You can get the form from our website, or I can mail one to you.
Okay, the website, I don't, hmm. Could you mail it? Wait, but if I need the form to ask for the form, how long is that? Because the other thing is, I think I need the certificate soon.
I understand. If I mail you a form, that adds a few days on the front end. The website would be quicker if you've got a computer or a printer.
My daughter has a printer. Oh, she's at her dad's though. Okay, never mind, let's see. So how long does it take once I send it in? The turnaround?
By mail, it's usually about a week or two once we receive it, depending on how busy we are. Mailing time on both ends is on top of that.
A week or two plus the mailing. So, like, three weeks? Or is the week or two already including the mail?
The week or two is just our processing. So yes, with the mail going back and forth, three weeks wouldn't be unusual. It could be faster.
Okay. Oh, hold on, I have to move, a lady is trying to get past me with the cart. Sorry. Okay. Now, because it's my mother, do I sign it as her or as me? That's what I don't get on these forms.
You'd sign as yourself, the person requesting. The form asks your relationship to the person on the certificate. Then your ID is the one that goes in the envelope, not your mother's.
My ID, not hers. Okay. But what if my last name is different than hers? I'm Wilcox, she's not Wilcox.

That's common, and it's okay. Your name on the ID won't match hers, but you'd list that you're her daughter. Whether we need anything extra to show the connection, I'd want to confirm with the records staff, since it can depend on the circumstances.
Hmm. So I might need extra paper? Like what, my own birth certificate? I thought I was just asking for one.
Possibly not. I don't want to tell you wrong. Let me put you on a short hold and ask the registrar's desk. Is that all right?
Sure, yes, go ahead. I'm just paying for these anyway.
Thank you. One moment.

Ms. Wilcox, thanks for waiting. They said a child can request a parent's record, and the form will ask for the relationship. They'll tell you if they need anything more once they see the application, and they'd contact you.
Okay, so they'd call me. So the form, ID copy, mail it, and then wait about three weeks. Is that right? I'm trying to write it down on the receipt, I don't have paper.
That's right. Do you want me to mail you the form, or will you download it?
Mail it, please. My daughter's printer is, well, it's complicated. It's Barbara Wilcox. Do you need my number too? It's four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-seven-six.
Thank you. And I'll need your mailing address for the form.
Oh. Um, I'd rather not say it over the phone from the store. Can I just get it off the website then? Is that okay?
Sure, that's fine. Just search for the city clerk's vital records page and the application is there. You can also stop in anytime if that's easier.
Okay. I think I've got it. Form, ID, relationship, three weeks. Maybe. Thank you, Owen.
You're welcome. Good luck with the smoke detector.
